findings.summary: The portal does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are pixel-identical; the page remains a bright white surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for surfaces, text, controls, and imagery.

findings.summary: Long animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched the preference but found three 7,000 ms animations and no reduced-motion CSS rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use prefers-reduced-motion: reduce to remove non-essential animation and make state changes immediate.

findings.summary: Text and controls include insufficient color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s axe-backed color-contrast audit failed; its overall accessibility score was 0.74.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text/control contrast to WCAG thresholds and verify normal, dark, high-contrast, hover, and disabled states.

findings.summary: Route, tab, scroll, and drawer interactions use legacy state changes rather than modern natural-interaction affordances.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition, animation-timeline, scroll-timeline, scroll-snap, or container-query support on the interaction-heavy portal.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained view transitions for route/tab continuity and CSS-native scroll/gesture feedback where it clarifies state; honor reduced motion.

findings.summary: Overlays and menus are custom div-based implementations rather than semantic top-layer primitives.
findings.evidence: The probe found 13 custom modal-class elements but zero dialog or popover elements; CSS implements fixed overlays and manual visibility.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal content and popover for non-modal anchored UI, with declarative controls, focus handling, Escape, and light dismiss.

findings.summary: A promotional reward interstitial obscures the primary portal content on load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360×800 screenshots show a large pink reward modal and backdrop blocking search, news, and navigation before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not show promotions before intent. Place the offer inline after core content or behind a user-initiated control, preserving a clear dismiss action.

findings.summary: The article template does not present a mobile-first layout at a narrow viewport.
findings.evidence: At a 360×800 capture, the article renders a dense multi-column desktop page scaled into the viewport, with very small text; its viewport declaration is only width=device-width.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a single-column article layout at narrow widths, fluid type/spacing, and a complete viewport declaration without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: Accessible names, semantic structure, and keyboard focus are unreliable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, image-alt, link-name, and accessibility-tree audits. The focus probe found many early anchors with outline:none, and the home probe found multiple empty H1 elements and unlabeled search inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control and link a discernible name, label search inputs, use one meaningful H1, preserve visible :focus-visible styles, and provide appropriate image alternatives.

findings.summary: The entry page is extremely slow and unstable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance was 0.03 with FCP 9.1 s, LCP 18.3 s, TBT 2,210 ms and CLS 0.921. The raw-CDP trace corroborated FCP 10.79 s, LCP 12.46 s, TBT 318.55 ms and a 320.79 ms longest task; layout measured CLS 0.43 mobile and 0.61 desktop.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer non-critical ad/analytics scripts, prioritize the LCP resource, reserve layout space, split long tasks, and establish CWV budgets in field and lab monitoring.

findings.summary: The page ships excessive, poorly prioritized script and third-party work.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 137 requests and 3.20 MB transferred, including 49 scripts (2.55 MB) and 2.05 MB third-party bytes. Confirmed head scripts top_index_libs7.js and top_index_com.js have neither async nor defer; cache and compression gaps are also present.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, load features conditionally, reduce tag duplication, compress dynamic responses, and apply durable cache headers to versioned assets.

findings.summary: Image markup wastes bytes and contributes to instability and accessibility gaps.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all 100 images missing explicit dimensions, 55 below-fold images without lazy loading, 40 oversized images, 44 legacy-format images, and 42 missing alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, lazy-load below-fold images, provide responsive modern sources, and add meaningful or empty alt values as appropriate.

findings.summary: The portal disables user zoom and has weak narrow-screen reflow.
findings.evidence: Home, services, and search templates set maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport. The article screenshot also shows tiny scaled desktop text at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions, then ensure content reflows and controls remain usable at 200–400% zoom.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime/platform errors and uses deprecated or recovery-hostile patterns.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console, deprecations (4 warnings), inspector-issues, bfcache, and valid-source-maps. HAR also recorded ORB-blocked scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve console and DevTools issues, replace deprecated APIs, make lifecycle handlers bfcache-safe, and publish production source maps securely.

findings.summary: Crawler and indexing signals are incomplete or inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and canonical audits. Recon found javascript:void(0) and HTTP links; /sitemap.xml returns 404; the home OG URL is HTTP; no JSON-LD is present. The no-JS crawler view exposes navigation but omits the main dynamic news content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real HTTPS hrefs, provide a sitemap, align canonical/OG URLs, add content-matching structured data, and server-render primary news/listing content.

findings.summary: Defensive response headers and cookie protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie audit found 11 cookies reported without Secure, including a session-named cookie, and several 400-day identifiers; all use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; set Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite according to purpose and shorten identifier retention.

findings.summary: The portal has a broad advertising and tracking footprint before user interaction.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 22 third-party origins and 10 known tracker domains, including DoubleClick, Taboola, Criteo, Google Analytics and Google Ads. HAR attributes 59 requests and 2.05 MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors and event collection, delay non-essential tracking until a valid consent/intent state, proxy where appropriate, and document retention and purpose.

findings.summary: Primary portal content depends on JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The crawler screenshot with scripting disabled displays a warning to enable JavaScript and leaves the primary news/content region empty, while the rendered screenshot contains a large feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core headlines and navigation, keep real links/forms functional without script, and progressively enhance personalization and tabs.

findings.summary: Search fields suppress browser input assistance and lack explicit labels.
findings.evidence: Home and search probes show search inputs with autocomplete=off and no associated label or aria-label; Lighthouse also reports naming failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide persistent labels and allow appropriate autocomplete/input assistance unless there is a documented security reason not to.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and inefficient assets create a disproportionate transfer and processing budget.
findings.evidence: The 3.20 MB load spends 2.05 MB on third parties, while image inspection found 44 legacy images, 40 oversized images, and 55 below-fold images loaded eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set page/third-party budgets, remove redundant vendors, defer background requests, and modernize responsive image delivery.

findings.summary: The portal’s search and service actions are not exposed as structured agent capabilities.
findings.evidence: DOM/source inspection found ordinary forms but no WebMCP or agentic tool registration; the public portal has actionable search and service-discovery surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, user-visible search/service actions as structured agent tools while preserving confirmation and permission boundaries.
